There are two ways to read: subscribe to the live CoT stream, or pull persisted data through the Marti API. Most integrations use both — the stream for "what's happening now," the API for "what's stored."

All paths below are under your TAK Server host; confirm exact parameters and response shapes in the spec. Every request carries your mTLS client certificate.

Live CoT (subscriptions)

To receive real-time events, you act as a TAK client: open the TLS streaming connection and you'll receive the CoT for the groups you read from. The Marti API lets you register and shape subscriptions:

  • POST /Marti/api/subscriptions/add — add a subscription.
  • PUT / DELETE /Marti/api/subscriptions/{clientUid}/filter — set or clear a server-side filter for a client (limit what's delivered).
  • POST /Marti/api/subscriptions/incognito/{uid} — subscribe without announcing presence.
  • GET /Marti/api/subscriptions/all (and related) — inspect current subscriptions.

What you receive is always scoped by your groups — you can't subscribe your way past access control.

Missions (Data Sync)

Missions are the main store of shared, structured content. To read:

  • GET /Marti/api/missions — list missions you can see.
  • GET /Marti/api/missions/{name} (or …/guid/{missionGuid}) — a mission's details.
  • Its contents (files, CoT, attachments), layers, logs, role, and subscription are exposed as sub-resources, e.g. GET /Marti/api/missions/{missionName}/subscription, GET /Marti/api/missions/{missionName}/role.
  • Subscribe to a mission to be notified of changes: PUT /Marti/api/missions/{missionName}/subscription.

Missions can be nested (parent/child) and protected by role, password, and keywords — all visible in the spec.

Roles & groups on a mission

Two things decide what you can do with a mission, and both surface in the API and in the Mission Manager UI (https://<server>:8443/Marti/MissionManager.html):

  • **defaultRole** — the permission a subscriber gets by default: ReadOnly, ReadWrite, or Owner. To read content you need at least ReadOnly; to write you need ReadWrite/Owner.
  • Groups — which TAK Server groups can see and subscribe to the mission at all (see Keycloak: identity & groups). Group visibility gates access before role does.

So "subscribe → read" works only if your identity is in a group the mission is shared to and your role is at least ReadOnly.

The RECON feed (Deploy App convention)

On a Deploy App / PVARKI deployment there's a standard server-wide mission called the RECON feed — for reviewed, verified intelligence that command wants everyone to see. By convention every user subscribes to it (read), while command/HQ roles maintain it (write). For an integration it's the obvious feed to subscribe to for a live picture of vetted friendly/enemy information — and, if your service is a command tool, the place to publish vetted observations. See the Takserver RECON feed and Mission Manager (Data Sync) wiki pages for the operator view.

Files & data packages (Enterprise Sync)

TAK Server's Enterprise Sync is a content-addressed store: every file is referenced by a hash. To read:

  • Fetch a stored file by its hash (the Enterprise Sync content endpoint — see the spec for the exact path/params).
  • …/Marti/api/sync/metadata/{hash}/… and /Marti/api/files/{hash}/metadata — read/set metadata, keywords, expiration for a stored object.

Mission contents typically reference Enterprise Sync hashes, so "list a mission's contents → fetch each by hash" is a common read loop.

Groups, data feeds & config (read)

  • GET /Marti/api/groups (and /groups/active…) — the groups you belong to / are active.
  • GET /Marti/api/datafeeds/{name} — inspect configured data feeds.
  • GET /Marti/api/inputs/config, GET /Marti/api/federationconfig, etc. — server-side configuration (admin-scoped).
